Himeji Castle, a symbol of feudal power, became a strategic center for clans seeking to gain influence. In The White Castle Duel, two clans compete to exert their influence in the White Heron's court, managing resources and building engines. On each turn, you will use their lamp tokens to obtain resources and activate actions. Among the actions available, you can buy and upgrade influence cards, place clan seals on gardens and training grounds, move your courtier between circles of influence, or trade with the Portuguese. These actions will allow you to accumulate a series of icons — flags, katanas, kabutos, and origami figures — that will reward you with points, and whoever ends up with the most points wins. [Rating: 3/10] Unfortunately broken mechanics.  Situations can arise (specifically in the second/retrieval half of the game) where a player can gain no benefit from their actions--not even take a default action to gain a modest benefit or a the ability swap tiles to open a path forward.

[Rating: 3/10] Pretty much everything I don't like in modern euro games. No interest in playing it again.

[Rating: 4/10] Collect 5 kinds of McGuffins that can be spent on 5 different kinds of actions, plus a 6th that takes any kind of McGuffin, and collect endgame scoring icons that score differently, and it's all Worker Placement with an attempted gimmick, and I mean... sure.  2+2

[Rating: 4/10] Bounced off this one hard. Incredibly fiddly on setup and play, the art and iconography are beautiful but blend together so it's a pain to see what's what.

[Rating: 5/10] 6 játékot próbáltam egy napon belül, messze ez volt a legkevésbé kreatív (bár az igazsághoz tartozik, hogy a többi mind könnyedebb kategória volt). Nekem ez egy nagyon erőltetett, öncélú pontsaláta volt így elsőre.

[Rating: 5/10] Bought without researching because everyone loved White Castle. I figured this one had to be a great, but quicker, version of that. We didn't like it because the decision space of each turn is overwhelming, and the game resources are extremely tight. It's a great game for a certain preference of player who wants silent contemplation while keeping 50 different option trees in their head at all times. But, it isn't for us.

[Rating: 5/10] Quite the letdown. The scoring is simply not variable and interesting enough. It gets old fast. You basically are collecting tags and trying to multiply them. There are however only two type of tags and how you get them just feels very narrow. The only thing changing game to game is how efficiently you can get the same tags. That is not enough for me personally. Too bad really because the action selection mechanism and how they translated it from the first White Castle game is actually well done. Overall though, I see absolutely no reason to play this instead of White Castle even if it is just

[Rating: 5.5/10] It's not a bad game, it just doesn't make sense to exist. The art style is still good, I just love the japanese theme and wooden accessories. I love the original White Castle, because of the complex decisions that can start a chain reaction. Oh, those chained actions, my boy! Well, in this duel game, you won't get that type of satisfaction. You just make a move, and that's it. It's just not as smart as the original, therefore I always prefer the original if I can choose.
